title: Rat.det_congr: the general-n determinant respects pointwise equality of matrices
statement: Rat.det is the determinant over the constructed rationals at GENERAL n, by cofactor expansion along the first row, over matrices encoded as functions Nat -> Nat -> Rat plus an explicit bound (F:rat-det-general-n-eq-det2 records the construction). This fact records that if two matrices agree at every index pair -- for all r and c, A r c = B r c -- then det A n = det B n, for every n. The hypothesis is POINTWISE and cannot be strengthened to an equation between the two matrices, because this kernel has no funext; the unhypothesized form is false. This is the lemma that unblocks induction over the dimension: det's recursive call is at the MINOR, so any such induction arrives at a matrix that is only pointwise the one the induction hypothesis is about.

formal.statement: theorem Rat.det_congr : ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : ((x1 : AxNat) -> ((x2 : AxNat) -> Rat))) -> ((x2 : ((x2 : AxNat) -> ((x3 : AxNat) -> Rat))) -> ((x3 : ((x3 : AxNat) -> ((x4 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} Rat (x1 x3 x4) (x2 x3 x4)))) -> Eq.{1} Rat (Rat.det x1 x0) (Rat.det x2 x0)))))

evidence.supports: Rat.det_congr is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.

evidence.supports: The statement still carries its pointwise hypothesis, and det genuinely depends on its matrix argument -- so the hypothesis is not discardable.
evidence.checker_command: cargo test -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib determinant_law 2>&1 | grep -cE '^test result: ok\. 2 passed'
evidence.notes: The count is tested, not just the exit status: `2 passed` fails if a test is renamed away or silently filtered out. The shape pin asserts the rendered type still applies the first matrix to two indices, which only happens inside the pointwise premise -- a statement that lost the premise would match neither. The non-vacuity control is that det (matMinor matId 0 1) 2 is NOT def_eq to Rat.one while det matId 3 is: two matrices built by the same machinery whose determinants differ, so det does not ignore its matrix argument and det_congr is not the trivially-true statement it would be if it did.

provenance.source: Lane determinant-laws, against ADR-1120's four open laws over the general-n determinant. Design note: ADR-1135.

notes: Two shape choices are load-bearing and neither is cosmetic. First, the dimension is quantified OUTERMOST and the two matrices live under the Nat.rec motive fun n => forall A B, (forall r c, A r c = B r c) -> det A n = det B n: the induction hypothesis has to be applicable at a DIFFERENT pair of matrices (the two minors), which it cannot be if A and B are fixed outside the induction. Second, the hypothesis is a Pi over two Nat indices rather than an Eq between two Nat -> Nat -> Rat values, because funext is absent here (positive control of the same kind, present: congrFun). The successor step is Rat.sumRange_congr on the two cofactor sums; the per-index obligation splits into the entry (h 0 c) and the minor determinant, and fun r c' => h (matSkip 0 r) (matSkip c c') types as the minors' pointwise premise because Rat.matMinor delta-beta-reduces to exactly that application -- no lemma is needed to bridge it. The base case is Eq.refl, both sides reducing to Rat.one.
